title: OmniCT: Towards a Unified Slice-Volume LVLM for Comprehensive CT Analysis
claim: A unified system combines a large multi-faceted dataset and a modular architecture, and beats baselines across diverse benchmarks.
layout: 3 rounded panels left-to-right: dataset stats, architecture flow, radar charts
description: A wide three-panel figure with pastel rounded backgrounds. Panel (a) shows dataset statistics for MedEval-CT as four charts: a nightingale rose chart of question types, a pie chart of slice vs volume data, a quadrant pie of clinical types, and a radial chart of organ types. Panel (b) is a simplified architecture diagram. A panda cartoon asks for a radiology report. A chest CT slice, a 3D volume and an organ render feed two modules, Spatial Consistency Enhancement and Organ-level Semantic Enhancement. Colored token sequences go into a Large Language Model box, which outputs a generated report to a panda doctor. Panel (c) shows two radar charts, one for slice-driven and one for volume-driven benchmarks. OmniCT is drawn in purple and compared with seven baselines listed in a legend.
caption: (a) is the statistics of the proposed MedEval-CT-Dataset. (b) describes the simplified architecture of proposed OmniCT. (c) shows that OmniCT consistently surpasses all baselines on both slice-driven and volume-driven CT benchmarks.
abstract: Computed Tomography (CT) is one of the most widely used and diagnostically information-dense imaging modalities, covering critical organs such as the heart, lungs, liver, and colon. Clinical interpretation relies on both slice-driven local features (e.g., sub-centimeter nodules, lesion boundaries) and volume-driven spatial representations (e.g., tumor infiltration, inter-organ anatomical relations). However, existing Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) remain fragmented in CT slice versus volumetric understanding: slice-driven LVLMs show strong generalization but lack cross-slice spatial consistency, while volume-driven LVLMs explicitly capture volumetric semantics but suffer from coarse granularity and poor compatibility with slice inputs. The absence of a unified modeling paradigm constitutes a major bottleneck for the clinical translation of medical LVLMs. We present OmniCT, a powerful unified slice-volume LVLM for CT scenarios, which makes three contributions: (i) Spatial Consistency Enhancement (SCE): volumetric slice composition combined with tri-axial positional embedding that introduces volumetric consistency, and an MoE hybrid projection enables efficient slice-volume adaptation; (ii) Organ-level Semantic Enhancement (OSE): segmentation and ROI localization explicitly align anatomical regions, emphasizing lesion- and organ-level semantics; (iii) MedEval-CT: the largest slice-volume CT dataset and hybrid benchmark integrates comprehensive metrics for unified evaluation. OmniCT consistently outperforms existing methods with a substantial margin across diverse clinical tasks and satisfies both micro-level detail sensitivity and macro-level spatial reasoning. More importantly, it establishes a new paradigm for cross-modal medical imaging understanding. Our project is available at https://github.com/ZJU4HealthCare/OmniCT.
